newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 7.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp plans to buy a 21.4 percent stake in South Africa's top car maker Toyota South Africa Manufacturing Ltd (TSA). Toyota currently has a technology tie-up with TSA, but does not own any shares in it. Toyota is negotiating with a local investment company which owns 27.8 percent of TSA, and the cost of the acquisition is estimated to total several hundred million yen. Nissan Motor Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Motors Corp are also expanding their businesses in South Africa.

Ito-Yokado Co Ltd plans entrust product transport to the Tokyo-based distribution unit of Kao Corp from April 1997 in an effort to cut distribution costs and increase efficiency in transport. The distribution unit, Kao System Butsuryu K.K., plans to initially deliver both its and other manufacturers' household products to 32 Ito-Yokado stores, mainly in Kanagawa prefecture which is adjacent to Tokyo.

Pioneer Electronic Corp plans to sell personal computers that work on both the Macintosh and Windows operating platforms from next spring, ending its policy of selling only Macintosh-compatible machines.
